newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end with modest gain despite golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end with modest gain despite golds.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished with a modest gain on Monday despite another dismal session for heavyweight gold shares.
The TSE 300 Composite Index edged 1.22 points higher to close at 5920.71. Almost 73 million shares changed hands for a value of C$1.04 billion (US$761.4 million).

The TSE posted gains in nine of 14 sub-indices, including base metals, forestry products, retailing and industrial products. But the strength was restrained by a 344-point drop in precious metals. COMEX spot gold prices have lost more than US$10 an ounce in the first three sessions of 1997.
Looking ahead, analysts said the late-December correction in Canadian equities may continue a bit longer.
"Day to day you may see marginal changes, but overall the market will continue its corrective phase in the near term," said Subodh Kumar, chief strategist for CIBC/Wood Gundy Inc.
In today's session, advancing stocks outnumbered declines 478 to 403 with 257 issues unchanged.
Among major gold producers, Barrick Gold Corp. fell C$1.45 to C$36.15 on 1.4 million shares. Placer Dome Inc. closed down C$1 to C$27.50 after earlier hitting a 52-week low of C$27.40.
Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan gained C$3.25 to close at C$120.50 on anticipation of strong prices for potash and nitrogen, two of the fertilizer company's main products.

Toronto-based real estate company Markborough Properties Inc. was among the most active stocks and jumped C$0.10 to C$0.57 in volume of 1.13 million shares following a favorable newspaper report that rated "the company to watch this year." The article said there is speculation Markborough may be a takeover target.
